title: Place rows before the query has to move them
description: Choose a dominant query, distribution style, and sort design. The fixed scenarios expose slice skew, join redistribution, block scanning, and replicated storage as separate costs.

workloads.label: Account dashboard
workloads.detail: Join a large sales fact table to accounts and filter recent time windows.

workloads.label: Fleet-wide rollup
workloads.detail: Scan and aggregate broad date ranges without one stable join key.

workloads.label: Shared product dimension
workloads.detail: Join one slow-changing 12 GB dimension to several much larger fact tables.

distributions.label: DISTSTYLE AUTO
distributions.detail: Start with automatic table optimization and verify its observed choice.

account-dashboard.title: Automatic is a sound starting point
account-dashboard.detail: Observe whether AUTO converges on a key that collocates the dominant account join before pinning a design.

fleet-rollup.title: Even placement protects broad parallel scans
fleet-rollup.detail: The scenario keeps work balanced when no durable collocation key dominates.

shared-dimension.title: Let size and workload evidence drive replication
shared-dimension.detail: AUTO can evolve a small table as it grows instead of fixing an ALL copy forever.

distributions.label: DISTKEY account_id
distributions.detail: Collocate rows with the matching account dimension, if the key distributes evenly.

account-dashboard.title: The large join is collocated
account-dashboard.detail: The modeled fact and account rows meet on the same slices while the key remains acceptably distributed.

fleet-rollup.title: The key adds little to a broad aggregation
fleet-rollup.detail: A fleet-wide scan still touches every slice, so monitor whether account skew creates a long-running slice.

shared-dimension.title: One table cannot collocate with every unrelated fact key
shared-dimension.detail: A shared dimension keyed to account_id still moves for joins on product or region.

distributions.label: DISTKEY tenant_id
distributions.detail: A low-cardinality or uneven tenant key can strand most work on a few slices.

account-dashboard.title: The chosen key creates skew and misses the join
account-dashboard.detail: The hottest tenant controls the stage while account rows still move across the network.

fleet-rollup.title: Parallel work is no longer balanced
fleet-rollup.detail: A broad rollup waits for the slice that owns the largest tenants.

shared-dimension.title: The small table pays both skew and redistribution
shared-dimension.detail: Replicating or leaving the automatic choice is a better hypothesis for this scenario.

distributions.label: DISTSTYLE ALL
distributions.detail: Copy the full table to every modeled compute node so local joins avoid redistribution.

account-dashboard.title: Replicating an 8 TB fact table is the wrong exchange
account-dashboard.detail: The join saves movement by multiplying storage, load, and maintenance work across nodes.

fleet-rollup.title: A full fact-table copy does not improve a broad scan
fleet-rollup.detail: Every node stores the entire table while parallel scan work still needs coordination.

shared-dimension.title: A small, slow-changing dimension can justify replication
shared-dimension.detail: Every fact-table join gets a local dimension copy, with a bounded storage and load multiplier.

sortDesigns.label: SORTKEY AUTO
sortDesigns.detail: Let automatic optimization learn from observed predicates, then inspect its actions.

account-dashboard.title: Automatic needs representative query history
account-dashboard.detail: Keep the dashboard workload visible long enough for observed predicate evidence to become useful.

fleet-rollup.title: Broad scans naturally skip fewer blocks
fleet-rollup.detail: A sort key cannot remove the need to read data that the query genuinely requests.

shared-dimension.title: The small table is not scan-bound in this scenario
shared-dimension.detail: Keep the design simple until query evidence shows a repeated selective filter.

sortDesigns.label: Compound event_time first
sortDesigns.detail: Order blocks by the timestamp used in bounded dashboard windows.

account-dashboard.title: Recent-window filters can prune most blocks
account-dashboard.detail: The leading sort column matches the selective predicate in the modeled dashboard query.

fleet-rollup.title: A year-wide rollup still reads most time ranges
fleet-rollup.detail: The sort order helps less as the requested interval approaches the full table.

shared-dimension.title: The dimension has no event-time predicate
shared-dimension.detail: A timestamp-first layout adds maintenance without pruning this query shape.

sortDesigns.label: Compound product_id first
sortDesigns.detail: Prioritize selective product filters before time in the modeled block order.

account-dashboard.title: The leading key does not match the dashboard predicate
account-dashboard.detail: Filtering only by recent time cannot use product-first block ranges effectively.

fleet-rollup.title: The broad rollup remains a broad scan
fleet-rollup.detail: Product ordering helps only when the query narrows products.

shared-dimension.title: Product lookup predicates align with the leading sort column
shared-dimension.detail: The modeled lookup reads a small range of the dimension blocks.
